identity.title: A High Cluster Formation Efficiency in the Sagittarius B2 Complex

paper_type_evidence.quote: (cite: Ginsburg2018a) observed the cloud with ALMA, obtaining a resolution of $0.5\arcsec$ in the 3 mm band.
Pyspeckit (cite: Ginsburg2011c) was used for the line fitting.

question.value: What fraction of stars in Sgr B2 form in bound clusters (the CFE), and is it consistent with environmentally dependent CFE models?

evidence.quote: We report a measurement of the CFE in the highest-density region in the Galaxy, Sgr B2, based on ALMA observations of high-mass young stellar objects.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2013.1.00269.S.

bands.value: 3 mm band, 0.5 arcsec resolution (data from Ginsburg et al. 2018)

evidence.quote: obtaining a resolution of $0.5\arcsec$ in the 3 mm band.
We have measured an additional 11 velocities from the H41$\alpha$ radio recombination line.

provided.value: 1.3 cm and 7 mm catalogs of H II regions (Gaume 1995; De Pree 2015)

evidence.quote: They detected 49 continuum sources. These are exclusively H II regions and components of H II regions.

what.value: Catalog of 271 ALMA 3 mm sources, 31 H II regions, and cluster census counts

evidence.quote: They reported a total of 271 sources spread throughout the cloud, of which 31 are confirmed H II regions

what.value: Gas masses and instantaneous SFE of Sgr B2 M and N

evidence.quote: give a gas mass of $M=9.6\ensuremath{\times 10^{3}}$ $\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$ in the Sgr B2 M cluster in their Table 2
Of the 32 unique H II regions within the field identified in the (cite: Gaume1995a) 1.3 cm data, 15 had measurements in (cite: De-Pree2011a).

what.value: CFE of 7 (+7/-3)% for the local neighborhood

evidence.quote: (cite: Lada2003a) reported a CFE of $\Gamma=7^{+7}_{-3}\%$ for the local neighborhood

simulations_or_models_as_data.value: Kruijssen (2012) CFE model, global and local versions, with Monte Carlo error propagation

evidence.quote: We obtain uncertainty contours on the model predictions by carrying out a Monte Carlo error propagation of the uncertainties on the observed parameters used as the input values.

what.value: Kroupa IMF extrapolation of the total stellar mass from observed objects

evidence.quote: We follow (cite: Ginsburg2018a) in extrapolating the total stellar mass implied by the observed objects using a (cite: Kroupa2001a) initial mass function.

what.value: ALMA data reduction and source catalog

evidence.quote: We note several ways the survey may be incomplete, which were described in detail in (cite: Ginsburg2018a)

unstated_but_needed: ALMA calibration and imaging details (all deferred to Ginsburg et al. 2018)
H41alpha line fitting setup (line model, initial guesses, baseline handling)
Exact Monte Carlo setup for the model prediction

method.value: Combine VLA and ALMA catalogs of H II regions and cores, extrapolate to total stellar mass with Kroupa IMF

evidence.quote: each H II region implies the presence of a total of 326 $\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$ of stars, while each 8-20 $\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$ core represents 135 $\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$

assumptions.value: Upper stellar mass limit of 200 Msun; each VLA source is an H II region with a star of at least 20 Msun

evidence.quote: assuming an upper stellar mass limit of 200 $\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$

analysis_steps.goal: Measure H II region velocities and velocity dispersion

method.value: Fit H41alpha lines, take standard deviation of V_LSR and compare with escape speed

evidence.quote: We measure the 1D velocity dispersion in Sgr B2 M by taking the standard deviation of the measured V$_{\rm LSR}$ values.

assumptions.value: H II regions trace stellar motions

evidence.quote: they closely follow the motions of their stars and serve as probes of the underlying stellar kinematics.

validation.value: Compared with De Pree et al. 2011 velocities (agree within 5 km/s except F10.37)

evidence.quote: Our measurements agree to within 5 km s$^{-1}$ with those of (cite: De-Pree2011a) for all sources we both measured except F10.37

method.value: Gamma = M_clustered / M_total from clusters M and N

evidence.quote: These values imply a CFE of $\Gamma=M_{\rm *,clustered}/M_{\rm *,total}\times100\% = 37\%$.

validation.value: Varied cluster membership and completeness; lower limit from source counts

evidence.quote: With 78 clustered out of a total of 297 sources, we obtain a CFE of $\Gamma>26\%$.

method.value: Predict f_bound from observed gas parameters, ignoring the cruel cradle effect, with Monte Carlo errors

evidence.quote: we only consider the bound fraction of star formation and omit the ‘cruel cradle effect’ (CCE)
Pyspeckit (cite: Ginsburg2011c) was used for the line fitting.
Plots were made with matplotlib (cite: Hunter2007a).
we adopt $\Gamma=37\pm7\%$

results_numeric.quantity: 1D velocity dispersion of Sgr B2 M, full data set

evidence.quote: Using the full data set, we obtain a higher $\sigma_{\rm 1D}\approx12~\textrm{km~s}\ensuremath{^{-1}}$.

results_numeric.quantity: Lower limit on CFE from source counts

evidence.quote: we obtain a CFE of $\Gamma>26\%$

findings_qualitative.value: The Sgr B2 M cluster is gravitationally bound, since sigma_1D is below the escape speed of 14 km/s.

evidence.quote: implies that the Sgr B2 M cluster is presently bound

claims.hypothesis: The CFE is constant in the Galaxy
claims.experiment: Measure the CFE in Sgr B2 from ALMA and VLA source counts and compare with the solar neighborhood
claims.finding: The CFE varies within the Milky Way

evidence.quote: Our observation therefore demonstrates that the CFE is non-uniform within the Galaxy.

claims.hypothesis: Environmentally dependent CFE models predict the observed CFE
claims.result: Predictions of 45–49% are slightly above the observed value but consistent within the errors
claims.finding: The model is consistent with Sgr B2

evidence.quote: The model predictions are slightly higher than the observed values, but they are consistent within the expected errors.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Excluding NE and S from the clusters; larger M cluster radius of 1.4 pc

evidence.quote: We therefore exclude them from the analysis

limitations_admitted.value: Completeness of the core catalog is hard to evaluate and depends on the models used

evidence.quote: For the less massive ‘cores’, the completeness is much more difficult to evaluate

referee_caveats_inferred: The CFE depends on the IMF extrapolation and on the assumed cluster boundaries
The error of 7% is a judgement of systematic effects, not a statistical error

code_released.value: Code is on GitHub: keflavich/SgrB2_ALMA_3mm_Mosaic and keflavich/SgrB2_CFE

evidence.quote: <https://github.com/keflavich/SgrB2_ALMA_3mm_Mosaic/> and <https://github.com/keflavich/SgrB2_CFE>

missing_for_reproduction: ALMA calibration and imaging details, available only in Ginsburg et al. 2018
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Tens of GB (3 mm ALMA mosaic), if reprocessing from scratch
reproducibility.score_reason: The code is public and the numbers are simple, but the catalog and processing come from the earlier paper.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: The main result depends on the catalogs of the earlier paper and on judgement about membership.

methods_papers.why: Source catalog and ALMA data processing
